limitations: These contracts record source inspection only; they do not prove ASEN runtime behavior or write parity.
Private-tag replacement is not a general secret detector.
expected_project is a caller ownership assertion, not authentication or tenant isolation.
Unknown write outcomes require readback and reconciliation; they must not be retried automatically.
Library UpdateObservation and DeleteObservation variants remain callable without expected_project.
Queue-helper invocation does not prove a durable queue row because local unenrolled projects skip insertion.
MCP forwards capture_prompt; the separately released Pi surface exposes but does not forward that option, and this core snapshot is not published-Pi proof.

cases.summary: A newly admitted observation is normalized, privacy-filtered, bounded, inserted with initial counters, and offered to the enrollment-aware queue helper.
cases.inputs: Session, type, title, content, project, scope, optional tool name and optional topic key; MCP also accepts legacy observation content.
cases.triggers: Invoke AddObservation directly, MCP mem_save, or HTTP POST /observations.
cases.preconditions: Post-redaction title and bounded content must be nonempty, and session ownership resolution must succeed.
cases.outputs: A new row returns its ID; HTTP returns 201 with id and saved status, while MCP reports the saved memory.
cases.durableEffects: A fresh sync ID and row use revision_count=1 and duplicate_count=1 with last-seen and update times; queue persistence depends on enrollment.
cases.negativeControls: Rejected empty post-redaction title or content creates no observation; queue-helper invocation alone is not durable queue evidence.
cases.privacy: Project is canonicalized, private-tag regions become [REDACTED], and content is UTF-8-safe truncated at the configured byte limit with a marker.
cases.assertion: Session ownership resolution precedes persistence; this case does not establish authentication.
cases.transport: MCP defaults type to manual, scope normalizes to project unless personal/global, may capture the current prompt, and HTTP requires session_id, title, and content.

cases.summary: A normalized topic key revises the latest undeleted row in the same project and scope.
cases.inputs: An admitted save with a nonempty topic key plus session, type, title, content, tool, project, and scope.
cases.triggers: AddObservation finds the latest undeleted matching normalized topic in the same project and scope.
cases.preconditions: Topic normalization yields a value and the ownership resolution and admission checks have succeeded.
cases.outputs: The existing observation ID is returned rather than allocating a new row.
cases.durableEffects: Session, type, title, content, tool, topic and normalized hash are replaced; revision increments while duplicate count does not.
cases.negativeControls: Deleted rows and same-topic rows under another project or scope do not match; no topic match continues to duplicate matching.
cases.privacy: Replacement title and content have already passed private-tag replacement and content bounding.
cases.assertion: Matching keys are normalized topic, project and scope, not title or content similarity.
cases.transport: The store behavior underlies admitted library, MCP, and HTTP saves; this fixture makes no live transport claim.

cases.summary: After no topic match, an in-window exact normalized-content identity collapses to the existing observation.
cases.inputs: An admitted save whose normalized content hash and exact project, scope, type, and title identify a recent undeleted row.
cases.triggers: Duplicate lookup runs only after topic lookup does not return a row.
cases.preconditions: The candidate creation time is inside the configured dedupe window.
cases.outputs: The newest matching existing ID is returned.
cases.durableEffects: Duplicate count increments with last-seen and update times; revision count and content remain unchanged.
cases.negativeControls: Outside-window, deleted, or differing hash, project, scope, type, or title candidates proceed to insertion.
cases.privacy: The compared hash is derived from already privacy-filtered and bounded content.
cases.assertion: Duplicate collapse uses all exact matching keys and does not replace the topic revision rule.
cases.transport: This store rule applies beneath admitted save transports; transport retries are not authorized by the rule.

cases.summary: The guarded update asserts owner inside the transaction and applies only valid project-immutable mutations.
cases.inputs: A row ID, required expected owner, and at least one supported field or paired literal find/replace mutation.
cases.triggers: Invoke UpdateObservationForProject through a guarded caller after transport validation.
cases.preconditions: Expected project resolves, row exists and matches it, project remains immutable, and find/replace is paired and not combined with content.
cases.outputs: A valid mutation returns the updated row; pure unmatched find/replace without metadata returns the unchanged row.
cases.durableEffects: A mutation updates selected values and normalized hash, increments revision and invokes enrollment-aware upsert; pure no-op does none.
cases.negativeControls: Invalid post-redaction values, absent owner, mismatch, absent row, project change, or malformed mutation leaves row, revision, and queue unchanged.
cases.privacy: Changed title/content and replacement results pass private-tag and nonempty checks; this is not general secret detection.
cases.assertion: expected_project is checked against stored normalized ownership inside the transaction and is not authentication.
cases.transport: MCP also checks current resolved project and directory fallback; HTTP maps malformed input to 400, mismatch or immutability to 409, and other misses to 404.

cases.summary: The guarded delete asserts owner atomically, then soft-deletes or tombstones before hard removal with enrollment-aware sync handling.
cases.inputs: A row ID, required expected owner, and optional hard-delete flag defaulting false.
cases.triggers: Invoke DeleteObservationForProject through MCP admin profile or authenticated-wrapper HTTP delete.
cases.preconditions: Expected project resolves and the selected row exists and belongs to it inside the transaction.
cases.outputs: Soft deletion records timestamps; hard deletion removes the observation after recording a tombstone and returns success.
cases.durableEffects: Hard delete orphans related memory relations instead of cascading; enrolled projects queue deletion, while unenrolled projects supersede prior mutation state.
cases.negativeControls: Missing owner, missing ID, absent row, or owner mismatch rolls back row, relation, tombstone, and queue changes.
cases.privacy: Deletion ownership is a caller assertion; conditional HTTP authentication wrapping is distinct and does not prove tenant isolation.
cases.assertion: The guarded entry requires expected_project, while the separate DeleteObservation library variant remains unguarded.
cases.transport: MCP exposes delete only in the admin profile and queues writes; HTTP delete uses requireAuth and maps malformed owner to 400, mismatch to 409, and missing row to 404.
